headline: 5 Essential Items Every Student Must Carry To Prove Their Delhi March Was Actually A 'Scenic Group Stroll'
body:
1. A laminated 'Leisure Activity' map clearly highlighting the route as a sightseeing tour of local barricades and police buses.

2. A bouquet of marigolds to be handed to the nearest officer to confirm the protest was actually a surprise flash-mob flower-gifting ceremony.

3. A pre-approved playlist of soft instrumental jazz that is legally required to play at 60 decibels to dampen any accidental chanting.

4. An official 'Pedestrian Tourism' certificate showing that you were just lost and looking for a reputable café, not advocating for policy changes.

5. A signed affidavit from your grandmother confirming that your presence on the road was simply a desperate attempt to find the best street-side chai in the city.
caption: Planning a casual stroll through the city? Better pack these essentials to keep your outing from becoming an 'illegal' march. #StudentLife #DelhiDiaries #ProtestPermits #StreetStroll (satire)
igHook: Which of these items are you keeping in your backpack for your next walk around the block?
imagePrompt: A close-up of a student backpack sitting on a city sidewalk, with various bureaucratic-looking forms and a small bouquet of flowers sticking out of the zipper.

sourceHeadline.title: No Excessive Force Used Against Student Protesters, Parliament March Was Illegal : Delhi Police To...

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 3 wins by introducing specific, absurd visual details (marigolds, jazz playlists, grandmother's affidavit) that create a warmer, more imaginative image of bureaucratic overreach compared to the dry, repetitive permit-list format used by the other candidates. It manages to satirize the premise without feeling like AI-generated filler.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses satire to comment on political protests and civil liberties without naming real individuals, targeting specific groups, or inciting hatred. The humor is generic and clearly framed as a satirical critique of protest regulation.
